content: 1. The school actively engages in regular communication and collaboration with stakeholders to support the Health-Promoting Schools (HPS) initiative. 2. The school systematically plans and monitors the implementation and performance of its policies and resources related to HPS. 3. A structured system is in place to ensure consistent planning and monitoring of the progress and performance of school governance and leadership in relation to HPS. 4. The school has made sufficient investments and allocated adequate resources to foster a safe and supportive social-emotional environment. 5. Resources, training, and funding are provided to maintain safe physical and virtual school environments. 6. Comprehensive school health services are integrated into school policies and aligned with national policies and regulations. 7. The school curriculum includes physical, social-emotional, and psychological aspects of student health, safety, nutrition, and well-being, aligning with national HPS policies. 8. The school curriculum promotes understanding, values, and attitudes that support sustainable consumption and environmental practices. 9. Pedagogical approaches and relationships between students and teachers, as well as among teachers, are designed to promote health, positive relationships, safety, physical activity, healthy nutrition, and overall well-being. 10. Training and support are provided to school staff to enhance health literacy and implement effective teaching strategies that align with the HPS approach. 11. The school leadership team, including board members, management, the principal, and other leaders, actively supports and promotes the ethos of HPS within the school community. 12. Leadership for HPS is distributed among the principal, leading teachers, administrative staff, school board members, health personnel, students, parents, and caregivers. 13. HPS leaders are offered professional development opportunities in leadership and HPS-related areas. 14. Students, parents, caregivers, legal guardians, and families are actively involved in all aspects of school operations related to HPS. 15. The school collaborates with local stakeholders, including government entities, through formal and informal partnerships to advance HPS goals. 16. School policies clearly define the desired social-emotional environment and include mechanisms for feedback and necessary improvements. 17. The social-emotional environment within the school is regularly monitored, and actions are taken to ensure a positive atmosphere. 18. School health services are tailored to the needs and priorities of the school and local community, with the flexibility to adapt to public health emergencies and emerging needs. 19. Investments in school health services include provisions for school nutrition and the availability of healthy food options. 20. Partnerships between schools and communities are strengthened through opportunities for regular reflection and review to ensure alignment with the adopted HPS framework. 21. Evidence is collected and synthesized to inform the design of HPS activities, ensuring they are contextually appropriate and evidence-based. 22. A national education policy or strategy recognizes HPS as a means to achieve national development goals through education and provides a framework for its nationwide promotion. 23. Leadership for HPS within the education sector is clearly established, with ongoing support and contributions from the health sector and other relevant sectors at all levels. 24. Local governments, communities, and schools collaborate and demonstrate formal commitments to the HPS initiative. 25. Systems are in place at national, subnational, and local levels to plan, monitor, and oversee the progress and performance of HPS initiatives. 26. Resources, including human, informational, and financial, are adequately allocated to ensure every school can function as a health-promoting school. 27. Flexible use of national funds is facilitated through grants and other mechanisms to support health promotion in schools based on their specific needs and contexts. 28. Opportunities are provided for professional learning on HPS, including models for releasing teacher time for such activities. 29. The content and delivery of the school curriculum are regularly planned, monitored, and revised to support health and well-being outcomes. 30. School policies ensure a safe environment for all members of the school community, aligned with national policies, and include regular equipment checks and other safety measures.
